title: Bernoulli switching lemma for CNF formulas
statement:
Let $f$ be a CNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge 1$, and suppose every clause of $f$ is proper: within any one clause, two literals sharing the same variable are equal, and no literal is repeated. Let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$, and in addition $p \le 1$. Draw a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$, which independently leaves each variable free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixes it to one of the two Boolean values, each with probability $(1-p)/2$; write $f\vert_\rho$ for the function of the remaining free variables obtained by fixing the assigned coordinates according to $\rho$. Then for every $t \in \bbn$,
\[
  \Pr_\rho\big[\,\mathrm{depth}(f\vert_\rho) > t\,\big]
    \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + e^{-np/3},
\]
where $\mathrm{depth}(g)$ denotes the least depth of a decision tree computing $g$.
hypotheses_covered: width of f at most w
within each clause, literals with equal variable are identical
each clause has no duplicate literals
replaced:
The same statement for a width-$w$ CNF $f$: under a Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction
with $0 < p \le 1/(40w)$ and $p \le 1$,
\[
  \Pr_{R_p}\big[\mathrm{dtDepth}(f|_\rho) > t\big]
    \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^t + e^{-np/3},
\]
obtained from the DNF version via the dual-DNF representation of $f$.
